surprises.description: Q3 sales were $638.1 million, above the preview’s roughly $625 million consensus. The preview expected about a 1-point price contribution in H2, but pricing contributed 2.5% to sales growth and drove almost all of the beat.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 net sales rose 2.3% year-over-year to $638.1 million, driven almost entirely by 2.5% pricing contribution while global volumes were roughly flat.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Revenue consensus was “$625.4M”; management had guided H2 pricing to “~1 point.”

surprises.description: Diluted EPS was $2.68, above even the preview’s highest cited consensus of $2.56, despite the preview’s warning that the Stockton land-sale gain had shifted out of Q3.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited diluted EPS consensus estimates of “$2.45,” “$2.56,” and “$2.53,” and said the Stockton gain “slipped out of Q3 into Q4.”

surprises.description: North America sales grew 3.8%, and management said volumes had outperformed single-family housing starts by roughly 400 basis points on a trailing 12-month basis. That is stronger than the preview’s concern that North American volumes might be flat to slightly negative, though the volume comparison is trailing rather than Q3-only.
surprises.fact_evidence: “North America net sales grew 3.8% to $502 million” and “volumes outperformed single-family housing starts by roughly 400 basis points on a trailing 12-month basis.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the Street was embedding “roughly flat-to-slightly-negative volume” and that investors wanted “flat-to-positive” North American volumes against starts.

surprises.description: Gross margin was 45.7%, below the preview’s watch range of roughly 46% to 46.5%, with higher material, depreciation, and freight costs; Wood Products margin also fell to 44.9% from 46.2%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Consolidated gross margin declined 40 basis points to 45.7% due to higher material, depreciation and freight costs, with Wood Products margin falling to 44.9% from 46.2%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch “consolidated GM ~46%” and gave a base scenario of “GM ~46–46.5%.”

surprises.description: Management reported steel costs up more than 50% year over year and at a four-year high, and said additional pricing actions would be announced soon. The preview had flagged rising steel costs and the pricing decision as issues, but not an increase of this stated scale or such near-term action.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Steel costs are now up over 50% year-over-year at a 4-year high,” prompting “additional pricing actions to be announced in the coming weeks, likely effective early January 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “rising steel prices” as a challenge and flagged “the pricing decision” and whether management would “push another price increase into an affordability-constrained market.”

surprises.description: The company raised the low end of its full-year operating-margin guidance to 20.0% from the previously reaffirmed 19.7%, while retaining the 20.5% high end.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 guidance was set at a 20.0% to 20.5% operating margin.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said FY2026 guidance was “19.7%–20.5%” and listed reaffirming that range as the base case.

surprises.description: Operating expenses fell 6.3% and SG&A headcount was down about 6%, showing cost savings and attrition leverage while the preview had identified the carryover of the cost-savings program as an open question.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Operating expenses fell 6.3% to $150.5 million (23.6% of sales versus 25.8%) with SG&A headcount down about 6%, reflecting cost-savings and attrition leverage.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “carryover of the $30M cost-savings program” as a 2027 issue to watch.

surprises.description: The Board approved a new $1 billion share repurchase authorization with no expiration, replacing the existing $200 million plan—far larger than the authorization the preview described.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Board approved a new $1 billion share repurchase authorization with no expiration (replacing a $200 million plan)” after $66.3 million of Q3 repurchases.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described a “raised $200M authorization” and a commitment to return “≥35% of FCF.”

surprises.description: Management said volumes were projected to be slightly lower for the rest of the year, adding a cautious near-term volume outlook even as it kept full-year margin guidance within the prior range’s upper end.
surprises.fact_evidence: “U.S. housing starts expected down low single digits and volumes projected slightly lower for the rest of the year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base scenario expected “volumes flat to −1%,” and its FY assumption was U.S. starts “down low-single-digits.”
